t0: The catalog could not be read:
t1: A policy is a set of rules every run it applies to must meet. There is no policy language to learn: each rule checks one thing, and the pipeline's authors cannot switch it off.
t2: What happens when a rule fails?
t3: The verdict is recorded and shown as a warning on the {run}; nothing is stopped. Use it to see how many {runs} would fail before you enforce.
t4: A failing rule stops the step (a {deploy:do}, an image push) or the run at its start, saying why. Someone with the right role can grant a time-limited waiver.
t5: Only deployments to these are judged by the {deploy:do} rules. Nothing ticked: every {environment}. Most teams scope {deploy:do} rules to production.
t6: {Environments}: only rules judged before {deploy:doing} can be scoped to {environments}, and this policy has none.
t7: Only runs of these branches. A run of a tag or a pull request has no branch, so it would not match. Empty: any.
t8: Only runs started by these. Nothing ticked: every {run}.
t9: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. It is shown wherever its verdict is.
t10: Production deployments need tests and a second person's approval
t11: Why the policy exists, in a sentence people will read when it stops them.
t12: Rules runs must meet. Nothing is created until you confirm at the end.
t14: When the warnings look right, set its mode to enforce on
